title: Rent Increase Notice Requirement
plain_language: Your landlord must give you 30 days' written notice before raising your rent by less than 10%.
requirement: Landlords must provide at least 30 days' written advance notice before implementing a rent increase of less than 10%.

coverage_conditions.description: All residential rental units in California.

citation: Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.4 or related CA statute
quoted_span: State law requires landlords to provide 30 days' written advance notice of rent increases of less than 10%.

title: California Statewide Rent Increase Cap
plain_language: Your landlord can't raise your rent more than 5% plus the cost-of-living increase, or 10%, whichever is lower, per year.
requirement: Landlords cannot increase rent by more than 5% plus the percentage change in the cost of living (or 10%, whichever is lower) in any 12-month period, based on the lowest rent charged in the prior 12 months. For tenants remaining in occupancy, increases are limited to no more than two increments per 12-month period.

coverage_conditions.description: Applies to residential real property statewide except: (1) affordable housing restricted by deed or regulatory agreement; (2) housing with certificate of occupancy within previous 15 years (unless mobilehome); (3) single-family homes or individually-owned condos where owner is a natural person and not a REIT, corporation, or LLC with corporate member; (4) owner-occupied duplexes.

exemptions: Affordable housing restricted by deed or regulatory agreement for very low, low, or moderate income tenants; Housing issued certificate of occupancy within previous 15 years (unless mobilehome); Single-family homes or individually-owned condos not owned by corporations, REITs, or LLCs with corporate members; Owner-occupied duplexes where owner occupies one unit as principal residence; Mobilehomes subject to different operative date (February 18, 2021)
interaction: Yields to a stricter local ordinance that covers the unit (stated in the source).
quoted_span: an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower

title: Just cause requirement for residential tenancy termination after 12 months of occupancy
plain_language: After you've lived there 12 months, your landlord must have a legal reason to evict you.
requirement: After a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential property for 12 months, the owner must not terminate the tenancy without just cause, which must be stated in the written notice. Just cause includes at-fault causes (default in rent, lease violations, nuisance, waste, criminal activity, illegal subletting, refusal of entry, unlawful use) and no-fault causes (owner or family intent to occupy for 12+ months, withdrawal from rental market, compliance with government habitability orders, intent to demolish or substantially remodel).

coverage_conditions.description: Applies to all residential rental properties except: transient/tourist hotels, nonprofit hospital/religious facility housing, dormitories, housing where tenant shares kitchen/bathroom with owner, single-family owner-occupied residences renting no more than 2 units, 2-unit buildings where owner occupies one unit, housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years (unless a mobilehome), certain individually-owned properties meeting ownership and notice requirements, and afforda

exemptions: Transient and tourist hotel occupancy; Housing in nonprofit hospitals, religious facilities, extended care facilities, licensed residential care facilities for the elderly, or adult residential facilities; Dormitories owned and operated by institutions of higher education or K-12 schools; Housing where tenant shares bathroom or kitchen facilities with owner who maintains principal residence there; Single-family owner-occupied residences, including accessory dwelling units, renting no more than 2 units or bedrooms, or mobilehomes; 2-unit buildings where owner occupied one unit as principal residence at tenancy start; Housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years (except mobilehomes); Individually-owned residential property not owned by a REIT, corporation, or certain LLCs, where tenants have received written notice of exemption; Affordable housing restricted by deed, regulatory agreement, or other recorded document, or subject to housing subsidy agreements
interaction: Yields to a stricter local ordinance that covers the unit (stated in the source).
quoted_span: after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.

title: California Assembly Bill 12: Security Deposit Limit (General Landlords)
plain_language: Your landlord can't charge more than one month's rent as a security deposit.
requirement: Landlords may charge only one month's rent for security deposits on both unfurnished and furnished residential units, except for small landlords who own two or fewer rental properties with four or fewer total residential units.

coverage_conditions.description: All residential rental units in California, except those owned by small landlords.

exemptions: Landlords who own only two rental properties with no more than four residential units total, if ownership is held by a natural person, family trust, or limited liability company (LLC) where all members are natural persons, may charge up to two months' rent for furnished and unfurnished units.
quoted_span: Starting July 1, 2024, many landlords may only charge one month's rent for unfurnished and furnished units

title: California application screening fee cap
plain_language: Your landlord can't charge you more than $30 to screen your rental application.
requirement: A landlord may charge an applicant a nonrefundable screening fee, but only up to $30 per applicant (adjusted annually for inflation starting January 1, 1998), and only to cover actual out-of-pocket costs of obtaining information such as credit reports and reference checks. The fee may be charged only if a rental unit is or will be available within a reasonable time, and only if the landlord uses a screening process that considers completed applications in order received or returns the entire fee to applicants not selected, within 7 days of selection or 30 days of application, whichever is first.

coverage_conditions.description: All residential rental properties in California.

quoted_span:
The amount of the application screening fee shall not be greater than the actual
out-of-pocket costs of gathering information concerning the applicant, including, but not limited to, the cost of using a tenant screening service or a consumer credit reporting service, and the reasonable value of time spent by the landlord or their agent in obtaining information on the applicant. In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant.

title: California Fair Housing: Protected Characteristics in Housing Discrimination
plain_language: Your landlord can't refuse to rent to you based on race, religion, disability, or other protected characteristics.
requirement: Housing providers cannot discriminate against applicants or tenants based on race, color, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial status, source of income, disability, veteran or military status, or genetic information. Housing providers cannot make written or oral inquiries about these protected characteristics, publish discriminatory notices, or aid in discrimination.

coverage_conditions.description: All residential rental housing in California.

quoted_span:
It shall be unlawful:
(a) For the owner of any housing accommodation to discriminate against or harass any person because of the race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial status, source of income, disability, veteran or military status, or genetic information of that person.

title: Prohibition on Common Pricing Algorithms in Restraint of Trade
plain_language: Your landlord can't use pricing software that uses competitors' data to set your rent.
requirement: It is unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination, trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce. It is also unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm if they coerce another person to set or adopt a recommended price or commercial term recommended by that algorithm for the same or similar products or services in California.

coverage_conditions.description: Applies to all persons and entities in California that use or distribute common pricing algorithms affecting rental housing prices or commercial terms.

exemptions: End consumers of products or services are excluded from the definition of "person" under the statute
quoted_span:
It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter.
(b) It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm if the person coerces another person to set or adopt a recommended price or commercial term recommended by the common pricing algorithm for the same or similar products or services in the jurisdiction of this state.

title: Annual General Adjustment (AGA) Cap at 5%
plain_language: Your landlord's annual rent increase is capped at 5%, even if the formula allows more.
requirement: Landlords of fully-covered rental units may raise rent each year by the Annual General Adjustment (AGA), which is capped at a maximum of 5%, even if the formula results in a higher amount. Landlords may still implement banked (unused) AGAs from previous years to raise rent to the rent ceiling.

coverage_conditions.description: Buildings with 2+ units where either: (1) certificate of occupancy issued before June 2, 1980, or (2) certificate of occupancy on or after June 2, 1980 AND unit is deed-restricted affordable housing. Landlords of fully-covered units may raise rent by the AGA (capped at 5% maximum per year), though banked AGAs from prior years can still be used to reach the rent ceiling.

exemptions: Partially covered units; Units exempt from the Rent Ordinance
citation: Berkeley Measure BB (2024), codified in Berkeley Rent Ordinance
quoted_span: The maximum AGA is 5%. This means that, if the formula in the Rent Ordinance results in an AGA that is greater than 5%, the AGA approved by the Board for that year can be no more than 5%.

title: Berkeley Annual General Adjustment (AGA) for 2026
plain_language: If you moved in before January 1, 2025, your landlord can raise your rent by 1.0% in 2026.
requirement: Eligible landlords may increase 2025 permanent rent ceilings by 1.0% for tenancies that began before January 1, 2025. Tenancies beginning on or after January 1, 2025 under Costa-Hawkins are exempt.

coverage_conditions.description: Multifamily buildings (2+ units) with certificate of occupancy before June 2, 1980. For tenancies that began before January 1, 2025, eligible landlords may increase 2025 permanent rent ceilings by 1.0% for 2026 under the Annual General Adjustment. Tenancies beginning on or after January 1, 2025 are exempt (covered under Costa-Hawkins).

exemptions: Tenancies begun on or after January 1, 2025 under the Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act
citation: Berkeley Rent Board Regulation 1148; Berkeley Municipal Code § 13.76.110A
quoted_span:
the Berkeley Rent Stabilization Board 
adopted the Annual General Adjustment (AGA) Order for Year 2026 which will allow 
eligible landlords to increase the 2025 permanent rent ceilings by 1.0% no earlier than 
January 1, 2026

title: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance - Multifamily Buildings Built Before 1980
plain_language: If you live in a multifamily building built before 1980, your rent is controlled.
requirement: Rent increases are limited under Berkeley's rent stabilization ordinance. Tenants in most multifamily properties built before 1980 are fully covered by rent control.

coverage_conditions.description: Multifamily properties (2+ units) with certificate of occupancy before June 2, 1980. Rent increases are limited under Berkeley's rent stabilization ordinance, and tenants are fully covered by rent control.

citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance
quoted_span: Most units in multifamily properties built before 1980** Fully Covered Yes Yes Yes Yes

title: Notice of Tenant Rights at Start of Tenancy
plain_language: Within 15 days of move-in, your landlord must tell you in writing whether rent control covers your unit.
requirement: For tenancies started on or after December 20, 2024, landlords must, within fifteen days of the start of the tenancy, provide written notice containing: the existence and scope of the Rent Ordinance; the tenant's right to petition against certain rent increases, if applicable; whether the unit is exempt from rent control; and any other partial exemptions. If the property has an interior common area, the landlord must post the notice there.

coverage_conditions.description: For tenancies started on or after December 20, 2024, in buildings with 2+ units that are fully covered by the Rent Ordinance (built before 1980 or deed-restricted affordable), landlords must provide written notice within 15 days containing: the existence and scope of the Rent Ordinance; tenant's right to petition against certain rent increases; whether the unit is exempt from rent control; and any partial exemptions. If the property has an interior common area, the notice must be posted there.

citation: Berkeley Measure BB (2024), codified in Berkeley Rent Ordinance
quoted_span: For tenancies started on or after December 20, 2024, landlords must, within fifteen days of the start of the tenancy, give the tenant written notice containing the following information: The existence of and scope of the Rent Ordinance; the tenant’s right to petition against certain rent increases, if applicable; whether the unit is exempt from rent control; and any other partial exemptions which may exist.

title: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance - Multifamily Buildings Built Before 1980
plain_language: If you live in a multifamily building built before 1980, your landlord needs a legal reason to evict.
requirement: Landlords must show just cause when evicting tenants in most multifamily properties built before 1980.

coverage_conditions.description: Multifamily properties (2+ units) with certificate of occupancy before June 2, 1980. Landlords must show just cause when evicting tenants in these properties.

citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance
quoted_span: Most units in multifamily properties built before 1980** Fully Covered Yes Yes Yes Yes

title: Owner move-in eviction relocation assistance payment
plain_language: If your landlord evicts you to move in, they must pay you $19,413 to help you relocate.
requirement: When an owner evicts a tenant for owner move-in, the owner must pay the tenant relocation assistance. As of January 1, 2026, the standard payment is $19,413 and the additional payment for qualifying households is $6,471.

coverage_conditions.description: All residential rental units in Berkeley subject to the Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance.

citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance
quoted_span: The Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance requires owners to pay tenants relocation assistance in the event of an owner move-in eviction.

title: Utility Charges Incorporated into Base Rent or Separately Metered
plain_language: Your landlord can only charge you for utilities if they're part of rent or separately metered.
requirement: For tenancies starting on or after February 6, 2024, a landlord may charge a tenant in a fully-covered unit for utilities only if the cost is part of the base rent or if the utility service is separately-metered and the lease requires the tenant to place the utility in the tenant's name. Landlords may petition the Rent Board to add average utility costs to the rent ceiling.

coverage_conditions.description: For tenancies starting on or after February 6, 2024, in fully-covered units (multifamily buildings with 2+ units built before 1980, or deed-restricted affordable), landlords may charge for utilities only if: (1) the cost is part of the base rent, or (2) the utility is separately metered and the lease requires the tenant to place the utility in the tenant's name. Landlords may petition the Rent Board to add average utility costs to the rent ceiling.

exemptions: Partially covered units; Tenancies started before February 6, 2024
citation: Berkeley Measure BB (2024), codified in Berkeley Rent Ordinance
quoted_span: For tenancies starting on or after February 6, 2024, a landlord may charge a tenant in a fully covered unit for utilities only if either: the cost of the  utilities are part of the base rent, or the utility service is separately-metered and the lease requires the tenant to place the utility in the tenant’s name.

title: Berkeley Rent Ordinance: Security Deposit Interest
plain_language: Your landlord must pay you interest on your security deposit each year.
requirement: For tenancies in units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance, landlords must pay tenants interest on their security deposit at the end of each year and a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before the end of the year.

coverage_conditions.description: Landlords must pay tenants interest on security deposits at the end of each year and a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before year-end. Coverage applies to units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance: (1) multifamily buildings (2+ units) with any certificate of occupancy date, (2) single-family homes with tenancies begun before January 1, 1996.

quoted_span: For tenancies in units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance, landlords must pay tenants interest on their security deposit at the end of each year and a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before the end of the year.

title: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance - Multifamily Buildings Built Before 1980
plain_language: In most multifamily buildings built before 1980, your security deposit must earn interest.
requirement: Security deposits must accrue interest for tenants in most multifamily properties built before 1980.

coverage_conditions.description: Multifamily properties (2+ units) with certificate of occupancy before June 2, 1980. Security deposits must accrue interest for tenants in these properties.

citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance
quoted_span: Most units in multifamily properties built before 1980** Fully Covered Yes Yes Yes Yes

title: Maximum Tenant Screening Fee
plain_language: Your landlord can't charge more than $68.96 for a tenant screening report.
requirement: Landlords may not charge more than $68.96 per tenant screening report (2026 amount; adjusted annually). Landlords must provide a copy of any consumer credit report obtained within 7 days, a receipt for the fee, an itemized list of out-of-pocket expenses and time spent, and refund any unused portion.

coverage_conditions.description: All residential rental units in Berkeley

citation: Berkeley Municipal Code § 13.78.010; California Civil Code § 1950.6
quoted_span: Prospective tenants should expect to receive a copy of their credit report within 7 days of receipt by the landlord, a receipt for the fee paid and an itemized list of any out-of-pocket expenses and time spent by the landlord on the screening, and a refund of any unused portion of the fee.

title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance – Criminal History Screening Restrictions
plain_language: Your landlord can't ask about or use your criminal history to deny you housing.
requirement: Housing providers cannot inquire about, use, or consider criminal history in rental advertising, applications, tenant selection, or decision-making. Providers cannot refuse to rent, terminate tenancy, demand higher deposits or rent, or refuse to add family members based on criminal history. They cannot disqualify tenants from rental assistance based on criminal history (with limited exceptions). If taking any action based on criminal history, the provider must give written notice and opportunity to respond.

coverage_conditions.description: All residential rental properties. Housing providers cannot inquire about, use, or consider criminal history in rental advertising, applications, tenant selection, or decision-making. Providers cannot refuse to rent, terminate tenancy, demand higher deposits or rent, or refuse to add family members based on criminal history. They cannot disqualify tenants from rental assistance based on criminal history (with limited exceptions). If taking any action based on criminal history, written notice and

exemptions: Lifetime sex offenders (limited exemption); Public housing/Section 8 properties (limited exemptions); Owner-occupied properties (1–3 units) where an owner of record resides as primary residence; Units under rental agreement allowing owner to move back (BMC 13.76.130 A.9); Units occupied by existing tenants seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates
quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.

title: Requirement to Accept Reusable Screening Reports
plain_language: If you provide a screening report, your landlord must use it instead of charging you.
requirement: If a prospective tenant provides a reusable screening report, the landlord must accept and use it instead of charging the tenant for a new screening report.

coverage_conditions.description: All residential rental properties. If a prospective tenant provides a reusable screening report, the landlord must accept and use it instead of charging the tenant for a new screening report.

citation: Berkeley Municipal Code § 13.78.010; California Civil Code § 1950.6
quoted_span: If the tenant provides a reusable screening report, the landlord must use it.

title: Prohibition on Sale or Use of Coordinated Pricing Algorithms to Set Rents or Manage Occupancy Levels
plain_language: Your landlord can't use software that uses competitor data to set your rent.
requirement: Landlords and vendors are prohibited from selling, licensing, or using coordinated pricing algorithms that use competitor data to set or recommend rent prices, occupancy rates, or other rental terms for residential dwelling units in Berkeley. Each month of violation and each unit affected constitutes a separate violation.

coverage_conditions.description: All residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley

exemptions: Products that publish aggregated and anonymous rental data without recommending specific rents or occupancy rates; Products used to establish rent or income limits per affordable housing guidelines of government entities; Products used solely for market research, appraisals, or software development and testing that do not use competitor data as input in real-time recommendations
quoted_span:
It shall be unlawful to sell, license, or otherwise provide to City of Berkeley 
landlords any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy 
levels that may be achieved for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.

title: Evictions for Non-Payment of Rent – Fair Market Rent Threshold
plain_language: Your landlord can't evict you for unpaid rent unless you owe more than the Fair Market Rent for your unit.
requirement: Landlords may not evict a tenant for non-payment of rent unless the amount of rent owed exceeds the Fair Market Rent (FMR) for the unit's bedroom size. FMR thresholds vary by bedroom count.

coverage_conditions.description: Non-payment of rent eviction restrictions apply to all RSO and JCO rental units

citation: L.A.M.C. – Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance (Non-Payment of Rent)
quoted_span: Effective March 27, 2023, landlords may not evict a tenant who falls behind in rent unless the tenant owes an amount higher than the Fair Market Rent (FMR). The FMR depends on the bedroom size of the rental unit.

title: Right to Counsel Notice Requirement
plain_language: Your landlord must give you a Notice of Right to Counsel when your tenancy starts and with any eviction notice.
requirement: Landlords must post and provide tenants with a Notice of Right to Counsel at the start of the tenancy, and also attach it to any eviction notice or termination of rental subsidy notice.

coverage_conditions.description: Right to Counsel notice requirement applies to all RSO and JCO properties

quoted_span:
Beginning August 20, 2025, landlords must post the
Notice of Right to Counsel
and provide it to the tenant at the start of the tenancy. The Notice must also be attached to a copy of any eviction notice or termination of a rental subsidy.

title: 'Mom and Pop' reduced relocation assistance for owner/family occupancy evictions
plain_language: If a small landlord evicts you to move in, you get $10,550 to $21,250 to help you relocate.
requirement: Landlords of 'Mom and Pop' properties (4 or fewer rental units, natural person owner with no more than 4 units total and one single-family home on separate lot in LA) may pay reduced relocation assistance for good-faith evictions for owner or eligible relative occupancy, provided: (1) building contains 4 or fewer units; (2) landlord has not used this provision in previous 3 years; (3) landlord owns no more than 4 units plus single-family home; (4) eligible relative does not own residential property in LA. Reduced amounts: $10,550 for eligible tenants, $21,250 for qualified tenants.

coverage_conditions.description: Buildings with 4 or fewer rental units owned by a natural person who owns no more than 4 units total (plus one single-family home on separate lot) in Los Angeles.

exemptions: Evictions not for owner or eligible family member occupancy; Landlord used this provision in previous 3 years; Eligible family member owns residential property in Los Angeles
quoted_span:
Mom and Pop properties may pay reduced relocation assistance payments to their tenants
for a good faith eviction for occupancy by the owner or eligible relative, provided that
requirements  in Section 151.30 of the LAMC are met.  This applies only for evictions  for
occupancy by owner, family, or manager.

title: Single-family dwelling relocation assistance under JCO
plain_language: Your landlord must pay you one month's rent as relocation assistance for a single-family home eviction.
requirement: For single-family dwellings subject to JCO owned by natural persons (including trusts/registered legal entities controlled by that person) who own no more than 4 dwelling units and one single-family home on separate lot, relocation assistance is one month's rent in effect when notice was served, payable as monetary payment or credit. LAMC 151.30(E) does not apply.

coverage_conditions.description: Single-family dwellings owned by natural persons with 4 or fewer total dwelling units (plus one single-family home on separate lot) in Los Angeles.

quoted_span:
When the residential real property  is
a single-family dwelling subject to the JCO and the owner is a natural person, including
natural  persons who hold properties in a trust or registered legal entity controlled by   that
natural person, who owns no more than four dwelling units and a single-family home on a
separate lot  in the City of Los Angeles: one month’s rent that was in effect when   the
landlord served the written notice to terminate the tenancy, as either a monetary payment
or credit.

title: Interest Payments on Security Deposits
plain_language: Your landlord must pay you interest on your security deposit.
requirement: The RSO requires interest payments on security deposits, with specific rules set by the Rent Adjustment Commission.

coverage_conditions.description: RSO-covered residential rental units built on or before October 1, 1978.

quoted_span: Interest Payments on Security Deposits

title: Report on Algorithm-Based Rent-Setting Software
plain_language: The city would study banning rent-pricing software; it isn't a rule for your landlord yet.
requirement: The Los Angeles Housing Department shall report on the number of ownership and management entities using algorithm-based software to establish rents and the feasibility of instituting a ban on such software in the City.

coverage_conditions.description: All residential rental units in Los Angeles where algorithm-based software is used to establish rents.

quoted_span:
MOVE that the City Council instruct the Los Angeles Housing Department to 
report on the number of ownership and management entities that are using algorithm-based 
software to establish rents and the feasibility of instituting a ban on the use of this software to set 
rents in the City.

title: Notice and Relocation Assistance for No-Fault Terminations
plain_language: If you're evicted through no fault of your own, your landlord must pay you 2 months' rent (3 if senior or disabled).
requirement: For no-fault just cause terminations (owner/family occupation, withdrawal from market, compliance with government orders, or demolition/substantial remodeling), the landlord must provide written notice at least 30 or 60 days in advance (as required by California law) describing the basis, stating the tenant's right to relocation assistance, and informing tenants of their right to receive an offer to renew if the property is re-rented for residential purposes within five years. Relocation assistance is two months of actual rent (or three months if tenant is senior or disabled), provided by direct payment or rent waiver, and must be delivered within 15 days of notice if by direct payment.

coverage_conditions.description: Same as just cause rule above; applies to residential rental properties subject to §98.0704 terminations for no-fault just cause.

exemptions: Same exemptions as just cause rule apply; If tenant is determined at fault for habitability violation triggering government order, tenant not entitled to relocation assistance under §98.0704(b)(3)
quoted_span:
(i) Unless section 98.0706(c)(1)(A)(ii) applies, the direct 
payment to the tenant shall be in an amount equal to 
two months of actual rent under the tenant’s lease in 
effect at the date of the notice.

title: San Diego Just-Cause Eviction: Relocation Assistance for No-Fault Terminations
plain_language: Your landlord must pay you 2 months' rent or waive 2 months' rent when evicting you for no-fault reasons.
requirement: When a landlord terminates a tenancy for no-fault just cause (owner move-in, demolition, or other qualifying reasons), the landlord must provide relocation assistance to the tenant at the landlord's option: either a direct payment equal to two months of actual rent (or three months if the tenant is a senior or disabled person), or waiver of rent through the end of the tenancy in that same amount.

coverage_conditions.description: All residential rental properties in San Diego covered by the just-cause eviction provisions of Division 7.

quoted_span:
Unless section 98.0706(c)(1)(A)(ii) applies, the direct 
payment to the tenant shall be in an amount equal to 
two months of actual rent under the tenant’s lease in 
effect at the date of the notice.

title: Prohibition of Anti-Competitive Automated Rent Price-Fixing
plain_language: Your landlord can't use software that uses competitor data to set your rent or occupancy rules.
requirement: Landlords may not use algorithmic devices to set rental rates or occupancy levels. No person may sell, license, or provide algorithmic devices to landlords. An algorithmic device is software that uses nonpublic competitor data to advise or recommend rental rates or occupancy levels.

coverage_conditions.description: All residential rental properties in San Diego.

exemptions: Software that publishes reports on rental rates or occupancy levels from aggregated historical data more than 90 days old or from publicly available information, without recommending future rates or occupancy levels.; Software used to establish rental rates or income limits under local, state, or federal affordable housing program guidelines.
quoted_span:
It is unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates
or occupancy levels for residential rental property.

title: San Francisco Annual Rent Increase for March 1, 2026 - February 28, 2027
plain_language: Your landlord can raise your rent by no more than 1.6% between March 2026 and February 2027.
requirement: For rent-controlled units in San Francisco, landlords may increase rent by up to 1.6% annually during the period March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027.

coverage_conditions.description: Rent-controlled units in San Francisco as defined by S.F. Admin. Code ch. 37. Coverage excludes owner-occupied buildings with two or fewer units and other exemptions under S.F.R.C. § 37.2(r).

predicate.reason: Source announces annual allowable increase for rent-controlled units under S.F. Admin. Code ch. 37 but does not specify building coverage criteria; coverage is determined by separate S.F.R.C. § 37.2(r) definitions of 'rental unit' and exemptions.

exemptions: Owner-occupied buildings with two or fewer units; Units exempted under S.F. Rent Control Ordinance § 37.2(r)
citation: S.F. Admin. Code ch. 37 (as administered by Rent Board)
quoted_span: For rent-controlled units, the annual allowable increase amount effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6%.

title: San Francisco Relocation Payments for Owner/Relative Move-in, Demolition, Capital Improvement, and Substantial Rehabilitation Evictions
plain_language: If you're evicted for an owner move-in or major work, you get $8,245 per tenant to help you relocate.
requirement: Tenants evicted for owner or relative move-in, demolition or permanent removal of the unit from housing use, temporary capital improvement work (20 days or longer), or substantial rehabilitation are entitled to relocation payments. The amount varies based on the date of service of the eviction notice and increases annually. As of March 1, 2026, the relocation payment is $8,245 per tenant, up to $24,733 maximum per unit, plus an additional $5,497 for each elderly (60+) or disabled tenant or household with minor children.
key_value: $8,245 per tenant; $24,733 per unit; +$5,497 for elderly/disabled/minor children (as of 3/1/26)

coverage_conditions.description: All residential rental units in San Francisco subject to eviction under these grounds.

exemptions: Temporary capital improvement evictions lasting less than 20 days are governed by California Civil Code Section 1947.9, not this ordinance.
quoted_span: Relocation Payments for Evictions based on Owner/Relative Move-in OR Demolition/Permanent Removal of Unit from Housing Use OR Temporary Capital Improvement Work* OR Substantial Rehabilitation

title: San Francisco Security Deposit Interest Rate
plain_language: Your landlord must pay 4.2% annual interest on your security deposit.
requirement: Landlords must pay interest on security deposits held for tenants at an annual rate of 4.2% for the period March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027.

coverage_conditions.description: All residential rental units in San Francisco.

quoted_span:
Security Deposit Interest:
4.2% for March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027

title: Prohibition on Algorithmic Rent-Setting Devices in San Francisco
plain_language: Your landlord can't use software that analyzes competitor rents to set your rent.
requirement: Landlords in San Francisco cannot sell or use algorithmic devices—software programs that analyze competitor rental data to recommend rent prices—to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units. Tenants or the City Attorney may sue to enforce this rule.

coverage_conditions.description: All residential rental units in San Francisco.

quoted_span:
The law prohibits the sale or use of algorithmic devices to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units in San Francisco.
The term “algorithmic device” means a device such as a software program that uses algorithms to analyze nonpublic competitor rental data for the purposes of providing a landlord recommendations on what rent to charge for a vacant unit.

title: Santa Ana Rent Increase Limit
plain_language: Your landlord can raise your rent by no more than 3% or 80% of the CPI increase, whichever is less.
requirement: A landlord can raise rent by no more than 3% of current rent or 80% of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) change for the year, whichever is less. The current maximum allowable increase for September 1, 2026 through August 31, 2027 is 2.87%.

coverage_conditions.description: All residential rental units in Santa Ana.

citation: Santa Ana Ord. (Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction)
quoted_span: The increase cannot be more than 3% of your current rent or 80% of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) change, whichever is less.

title: Rent increase cap at 3% or 80% CPI (whichever is lower)
plain_language: Your landlord can raise your rent by no more than 3% or 80% of the CPI change, whichever is lower.
requirement: Residential rent increases are limited annually to the lower of 3% or 80% of the Consumer Price Index change over the prior 12 months. If CPI is negative, no increase is permitted.

coverage_conditions.description: Applies to residential buildings with a certificate of occupancy before February 1, 1995. Exempts buildings constructed on or after February 1, 1995 and mobile home spaces.

exemptions: Buildings with certificate of occupancy on or after February 1, 1995; Mobile home spaces offered for rent after January 1, 1990
quoted_span: Increase in residential rents are limited to the lower of 3% per year, or 80% of the percent change in the Consumer Price Index over the most recent 12-month period. If the CPI is negative, no rent increase is permitted.

title: Relocation assistance or rent waiver for no-fault termination
plain_language: Your landlord must pay you 3 months' relocation assistance or waive 3 months' rent when ending your tenancy without cause.
requirement: When terminating a tenancy for no-fault just cause (owner occupancy, removal from rental market, or demolition/substantial remodel), the landlord must provide either three months of relocation assistance or waive rent payment for the final three months of tenancy.
key_value: 3 months relocation assistance or 3 months rent waiver

coverage_conditions.description: Applies to residential rental buildings not constructed in the last 15 years and not deed-restricted as affordable housing.

exemptions: Housing produced within the last 15 years; Deed-restricted affordable housing; Hotel and transient occupancy; Hospital and care facilities; Dormitories and shared living quarters
citation: Santa Ana Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
quoted_span: Under a no-fault just cause termination, the owner shall either provide 3 months of relocation assistance or waive payment of rent for the final 3 months of the tenancy.

title: Santa Ana Just Cause Eviction Requirement
plain_language: Your landlord must have a valid reason, like non-payment of rent, to evict you.
requirement: A landlord must have a valid reason to evict a tenant, such as non-payment of rent, breach of lease, or the landlord's intent to occupy the property themselves.

coverage_conditions.description: All residential rental units in Santa Ana.

citation: Santa Ana Ord. (Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction)
quoted_span: Your landlord must have a valid reason to evict you. This could be for not paying rent, breaking the lease, or if the landlord wants to move into the property themselves.

title: Initiative Petition 25-21: Limit on Annual Rent Increases
plain_language: A proposed cap on your rent increases (5% or inflation, whichever is lower) did not become law.
requirement: The proposed law would limit annual rent increases for residential dwelling units to the lower of the annual increase in the Consumer Price Index or five percent. The proposal was struck down by the Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court as violating the state constitution's prohibition on initiative petitions relating to religion, because it exempted facilities operated solely for religious purposes.

coverage_conditions.description: All residential dwelling units except: owner-occupied buildings with four or fewer units; units whose rents are subject to regulation by a public authority (excluding mobile housing voucher programs); units rented to transient guests for less than 14 consecutive days; units in facilities operated solely for educational, religious, or non-profit purposes; and units with first residential certificate of occupancy less than 10 years old.

args.reason: dwelling units rented to transient guests for periods under 14 consecutive days

exemptions: Owner-occupied buildings with four or fewer units; Dwelling units regulated by public authority (excluding mobile housing vouchers); Transient rentals under 14 consecutive days; Facilities operated solely for educational, religious, or non-profit purposes; Units with certificate of occupancy less than 10 years old
citation: Initiative Petition 25-21; M.G.L. c. 40P (existing prohibition on rent control)
quoted_span:
the annual increase in Consumer 
Price Index or [five percent], whichever is lower.

title: State prohibition on local rent control, with limited exceptions
plain_language: Your city or town can't put rent control on your apartment.
requirement: Massachusetts prohibits any city or town from enacting, maintaining or enforcing rent control of any kind. However, a city or town that accepts chapter 40P may adopt rent control regulation only if: (a) compliance is entirely voluntary after six months; (b) the regulation does not cover occupancy, services, evictions, condominium conversion, or removal from the program, and does not apply to units owned by an entity owning fewer than ten rental units or units with fair market rent exceeding $400; and (c) the municipality compensates owners from general funds for the difference between fair market rent and controlled rent.

coverage_conditions.description: All residential rental units in Massachusetts cities and towns.

exemptions: Units owned by a person or entity owning fewer than ten rental units; Rental units with fair market rent exceeding $400
interaction: May preempt local ordinances on the same subject; flagged for review.
quoted_span:
No city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind, except that any city or town that accepts this chapter may adopt rent control regulation that provides:
(a) after six months from the date of the initial adoption of rent control regulation by a particular city or town, compliance on the part of property owners as to the rent control regulation or any subsequently adopted rent control regulation shall be entirely voluntary and uncoerced
conflict_note: Possible preemption of local ordinances; needs human review.

title: Nonpayment of Rent—Notice to Quit and Eviction
plain_language: Your landlord must give you 14 days' written notice before evicting you for not paying rent.
requirement: A landlord must give a tenant 14 days' written notice to quit for nonpayment of rent. The tenant may stop the eviction by paying all rent due, interest, and court costs on or before the answer is due in the eviction action. If the nonpayment was caused by a government agency's failure to deliver a subsistence or rental payment to the tenant or landlord, the court must continue the hearing at least 7 days to notify the agency, and the tenancy is treated as not terminated if the tenant tenders all rent, interest and costs within that time.

coverage_conditions.description: All residential rental housing with a written lease.

quoted_span: Upon the neglect or refusal to pay the rent due under a written lease, fourteen days' notice to quit, given in writing by the landlord to the tenant, shall be sufficient to determine the lease, unless the tenant, on or before the day the answer is due, in an action by the landlord to recover possession of the premises, pays or tenders to the landlord or to his attorney all rent then due, with interest and costs of suit.

title: Security deposit maximum and prepaid rent limits
plain_language: Your landlord can't charge more than one month's rent as a security deposit.
requirement: A landlord may require tenants to pay at most: first month's rent, last month's rent at the same rate, and a security deposit equal to one month's rent (or a fee in lieu of deposit under executive office regulations, not to exceed one month's rent total). Landlords may also charge for key and lock installation.

coverage_conditions.description: All residential rental properties, except those with tenancies of 100 days or less for vacation or recreational purposes.

exemptions: Tenancies of 100 days or less for vacation or recreational purposes
quoted_span:
At or prior to the commencement of any tenancy, no lessor or agent of the lessor may require a tenant or prospective tenant to pay, to the lessor or to an agent of the lessor, any amount in excess of the following:
(i) rent for the first full month of occupancy;  and,
(ii) rent for the last full month of occupancy calculated at the same rate as the first month;  and,
(iii) a security deposit equal to the first month's rent

title: Ban on rent-pricing algorithms and coordination services
plain_language: Your landlord can't use rent-pricing software that pools competitors' data to set your rent.
requirement: Landlords cannot contract with or pay for services that collect actual rent prices, analyze them, and recommend rental prices to landlords. Service providers cannot help landlords agree not to compete on rent pricing for residential units.

coverage_conditions.description: All residential dwelling units in Massachusetts, excluding inpatient medical care, licensed long-term care, and detention or correctional facilities.

exemptions: Publication of fair market rent calculated using publicly available data does not constitute a prohibited recommendation
quoted_span: No real estate lessor, or any agent or subcontractor thereof, shall subscribe to, contract with or otherwise exchange anything of value in return for the services of a service provider.

title: An Act prohibiting algorithmic rent setting
plain_language: Your landlord can't use algorithmic rent setting to determine your rent.
requirement: This bill proposes to prohibit the use of algorithmic rent setting in the rental housing market.

coverage_conditions.description: All residential rental housing in Massachusetts.

quoted_span: An Act prohibiting algorithmic rent setting

title: Housing Stability Notification Act – Notice requirement when ending tenancy
plain_language: Your landlord must give you tenants' rights information when ending your tenancy.
requirement: When a landlord ends a tenancy or decides not to renew a lease, the landlord must provide the tenant with a Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources at the same time as the Notice to Quit or Notice of Non-renewal. The landlord must also send a copy of the notice and a Certificate of Compliance/Service to the City of Boston's Office of Housing Stability.

coverage_conditions.description: Applies to all residential units in the City of Boston, except those in hospitals, skilled nursing facilities, health facilities, or non-profit facilities providing short-term treatment for substance abuse.

args.reason: hospital, skilled nursing facility or health facility
non-profit facility whose primary purpose is providing short-term treatment, assistance or therapy for alcohol, drug, or other substance abuse

exemptions: Hospital, skilled nursing facility or health facility residences; Non-profit facility residences whose primary purpose is providing short-term treatment, assistance or therapy for alcohol, drug, or other substance abuse
citation: Boston City Ordinance, Housing Stability Notification Act (Sec. 10-11.7)
quoted_span:
The HSNA requires that landlords give this Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources
to tenants when the landlord starts the eviction process, or when the landlord
decides to not offer the tenant a renewal of their lease agreement. The Notice of
Tenants’ Rights and Resources must be delivered at the same time as the Notice to
Quit.

title: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy—Criminal History Screening Restrictions
plain_language: If your housing is city-funded or income-restricted, your landlord can't reject you over an arrest record.
requirement: Housing providers receiving DND funding, land, or having income-restricted units created under BPDA's Inclusionary Development Policy must not impose a blanket policy denying housing based on arrests or convictions. Providers must consider applicants on a case-by-case basis and may not consider arrests without conviction, convictions subject to judicial relief, juvenile records, or convictions over 5 years old—unless there is a direct relationship between the conviction and housing sought or unreasonable risk of substantial harm to others' safety.

coverage_conditions.description: This policy applies to multifamily residential buildings where the housing provider receives DND funding/land or has income-restricted units created under BPDA's Inclusionary Development Policy. The screening restrictions cover all units in qualifying buildings.

exemptions: Convictions with a direct relationship to the housing sought or unreasonable risk of substantial harm to others' safety may be considered.; Current criminal behavior is excluded from the policy's protections.; Federal or state law imposing criminal history requirements preempts this policy.
citation: Boston Department of Neighborhood Development, Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (Feb. 2017)
quoted_span:
Housing providers receiving Department of Neighborhood Development (DND) funding and/or 
land, or that have income restricted units created under the Boston Planning and Development 
Agency (BPDA) Inclusionary Development Policy will not impose a blanket policy that denies 
housing to anyone with arrests and or convictions. Housing providers will consider applicants on 
a case-by-case basis.

title: Failure to Pay Rent—Eviction Cause
plain_language: Your landlord must give you 14 days' notice before evicting you for nonpayment if you live in federally subsidized housing.
requirement: A landlord may evict a tenant for failure to pay rent. Landlord need not give notice before filing suit unless tenant resides in federally subsidized housing, in which case landlord must give 14-day notice. Tenant cannot be evicted for nonpayment if tenant paid utilities to prevent service disconnection when landlord was responsible for payment.

coverage_conditions.description: All residential rental units in New Jersey

exemptions: Federally subsidized housing tenants
quoted_span:
The landlord is not required to give the tenant notice before filing an 
eviction suit, except if the tenant resides in federally subsidized housing.

title: Safe Housing Act - Lease termination due to domestic violence
plain_language: You can end your lease with 30 days' notice if you're a victim of domestic violence.
requirement: A tenant who is a victim of domestic violence or whose child faces an imminent threat of serious physical harm from a specific person may terminate their lease with 30 days' notice after providing the landlord with documented proof of domestic violence (such as a restraining order, law enforcement record, medical documentation, or certification from a domestic violence specialist). The tenant's security deposit must be returned within 15 business days.

coverage_conditions.description: Applies to all residential rental properties except transient or seasonal rentals.

exemptions: Transient or seasonal rentals
quoted_span:
Lease Termination due to domestic violence shall take effect on the thirtieth day following 
receipt by the landlord of one of the documents listed above and a written notice from the tenant 
that they intend to vacate the premises and terminate the lease.

title: Security Deposit Law - Maximum deposit and prohibited practices
plain_language: Your landlord can't charge more than one and one-half months' rent as a security deposit.
requirement: A landlord may not collect more than one and one-half times the tenant's monthly rent as a security deposit. Combined with first month's rent, the landlord may not require more than two and one-half times the monthly rent at lease inception. Any prepaid funds (including last month's rent) held to secure future rents count toward the security deposit limit. Pet security deposits cannot exceed one and one-half times monthly rent when combined with the regular security deposit.

coverage_conditions.description: Applies to all residential rental properties except owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings, unless the tenant requests application of the law in writing 30 days after occupancy.

exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings (unless tenant requests application)
quoted_span:
Any additional 
yearly security deposit increase may not exceed 10% of the current security deposit.

title: Residential Rental Property Application Fee Cap
plain_language: Your landlord can't charge more than $50 to apply for a rental.
requirement: A landlord or agent cannot charge an application or similar fee to apply to lease or sublease residential rental property that exceeds $50. The cap is adjusted annually by the Consumer Price Index.

coverage_conditions.description: All residential rental properties except one-family or two-family dwellings offered for rent.

exemptions: One-family or two-family dwelling offered for rent; Real estate licensees unless the licensee is the landlord
quoted_span:
A landlord, or
agent thereof, shall not require an application or other similar fee to apply
to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes, which
exceeds $50.

title: Discrimination in rental housing
plain_language: Your landlord can't refuse to rent to you based on race, sex, disability, or other protected characteristics.
requirement: It is illegal for a landlord to refuse to rent or discriminate in rental of housing based on race, creed, color, national origin, ancestry, sex, marital status, civil union status, domestic partnership status, familial status, affectional or sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, mental and physical disability, nationality, or source of lawful income. A landlord may refuse to rent only if the prospective tenant lacks sufficient income, the family is too large for the unit, occupancy would violate zoning laws, or has poor credit history.

coverage_conditions.description: Applies to all landlord-tenant relationships except two-family owner-occupied dwellings, rooms in owner- or resident-occupied single homes, and residences planned exclusively for one sex.

exemptions: Two-family owner-occupied dwellings; Rooms in owner- or resident-occupied single homes; Residences planned exclusively for one sex (e.g., YMCA, age-restricted housing for familial status purposes)
quoted_span:
The New Jersey Law Against Discrimination (LAD), 
N.J.S.A. 10:5-12(g) to -(h), prohibits discrimination when selling or renting property and requires 
equal treatment in the sale or rental of housing regardless of race, creed, color, national origin, 
ancestry, sex, marital status, civil union status, domestic partnership status, familial status, 
affectional or sexual orientation, gender  identity or expression, mental and physical disability, 
nationality, or source of lawful income.

title: Fair Chance in Housing Act: Criminal record screening restrictions
plain_language: Your landlord can't ask about your criminal record until after offering you the apartment.
requirement: Housing providers cannot inquire about an applicant's criminal record before making a conditional offer. After a conditional offer, they may only consider certain convictions (murder, aggravated sexual assault, kidnapping, arson, human trafficking, sex offenses with lifetime registration, or indictable offenses issued or with prison sentence concluded within specified timeframes: 6 years for 1st degree, 4 years for 2nd/3rd degree, 1 year for 4th degree). They must conduct an individualized assessment considering offense nature/severity, applicant age, time elapsed, rehabilitation evidence, impact on tenant safety, and whether offense occurred on rented property. They cannot consider arrests

coverage_conditions.description: All rental dwelling units except owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.

exemptions: Drug-related criminal activity for the manufacture or production of methamphetamine on the premises of federally assisted housing; Whether the applicant is subject to a lifetime registration requirement under a State sex offender registration program
quoted_span:
A housing
provider
shall not make any oral or written inquiry
regarding an applicant’s criminal record prior to making a conditional offer.

title: Prohibition on Algorithmic Rent-Setting and Coordination
plain_language: Your landlord can't use algorithms to coordinate rental prices with other landlords.
requirement: Landlords and property management companies cannot use algorithmic devices or software to set, recommend, or coordinate rental prices among multiple properties. It is unlawful for landlords to use coordinating functions, for coordinators to facilitate parallel pricing coordination, or for any person to perform a coordinating function that collects competitively sensitive information (such as rental prices or lease terms) from multiple property owners to set or recommend rents.

coverage_conditions.description: All residential rental dwellings in New Jersey, except those subject to affordability controls or exempt coordinating functions (such as real estate brokerages, research databases, or public rent-setting programs).

exemptions: Properties subject to affordability controls (federal Section 8, state housing programs, rent control or rent leveling ordinances, or other government housing programs); Coordinating functions involving only research, statistical analysis, or testing where competitively sensitive information is not used in setting rents; Public rent estimates available at no cost; Real estate brokerage databases available on equal terms that do not collect competitively sensitive information to set rents; Government entities setting rents through affordability controls
interaction: May preempt local ordinances on the same subject; flagged for review.
quoted_span:
It
shall be unlawful and a violation of the “New Jersey Antitrust Act,” P.L.1970,
c.73 (C.56:9-1 et seq.) for:
a.     a rental property owner, or any agent,
representative, or subcontractor thereof, to receive, subscribe to, contract
for, or otherwise exchange any form of consideration in return for the use of,
the services of a coordinator;
b.    a coordinator to facilitate a tacit or express
agreement among rental property owners that restricts competition with respect
to residential dwelling units, including by performing a coordinating
function;
c.     two or more persons to engage in

or
otherwise facilitate

parallel pricing coordination
conflict_note: Possible preemption of local ordinances; needs human review.

title: Prohibition Against Algorithmic Rent-Fixing in the Rental Housing Market
plain_language: Your landlord can't use software to share competitor data to set rental prices.
requirement: Landlords in Hoboken are prohibited from using software, algorithms, or data-sharing platforms to collect and analyze nonpublic competitor information from other landlords in order to coordinate, recommend, or implement rental prices, lease terms, or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units.

coverage_conditions.description: All residential dwelling units in Hoboken, excluding medical/long-term care or detention facilities.

arg.reason: Ordinance excludes medical/long-term care or detention facilities, which are not residential rental apartment buildings

exemptions: Medical or long-term care facilities; Detention facilities
quoted_span: Landlords who rent any residential dwelling unit (defined as any primary residence excluding medical/long-term care or detention facilities) in the City of Hoboken are prohibited from price fixing using algorithmic pricing. For purposes of this chapter, “price fixing using algorithmic pricing”shall be defined as the use of software, algorithms, or data-sharing platforms to collect and analyze nonpublic competitor information from other real estate lessors in order to coordinate, recommend, or implement rental prices, lease terms, or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units among competing real estate lessors.

title: Jersey City Rent Control Ordinance
plain_language: If your building is under rent control, your rent increases are limited.
requirement: Jersey City enforces a rent control ordinance that regulates rent increases for residential rental properties. The Office of Landlord/Tenant Relations administers and enforces Chapter 260 of the Jersey City Municipal Code, which provides a rent control framework with certain exemptions and allows for capital improvement increases, vacancy increases, and hardship increases through formal applications.

coverage_conditions.description: Applies to residential rental buildings with five or more units. Exempt: 1-4 unit properties.

exemptions: Single-family and small multifamily buildings (1-4 units)
quoted_span:
The Office of Landlord Tenant Relations administers and enforces the
Rent Control Ordinance, Chapter 260
of the Jersey City Municipal Code

title: Prohibition on Algorithmic Rent-Fixing and Coordination Among Landlords
plain_language: Your landlord can't use software to coordinate rental prices with other landlords.
requirement: Landlords and service providers are prohibited from using software or coordinating to collect nonpublic competitor information (prices, supply levels, occupancy rates, lease terms) from multiple landlords and using it to recommend rent prices, lease terms, or occupancy levels. Service providers cannot facilitate agreements among landlords not to compete on rental pricing or other rental terms.

coverage_conditions.description: All residential dwelling units in Jersey City, including houses, apartments, and accessory units (excludes inpatient medical care, long-term care, detention or correctional facilities). Exemption: single-property owners taking actions only on their own multiple properties.

exemptions: Actions of owners related exclusively to properties controlled by the same rental property owner; Licensed real estate agents operating in accordance with applicable state regulations
citation: Jersey City Ord. 25-057, Jersey City Municipal Code § 218-12
quoted_span:
No service provider shall facilitate an agreement not to compete among real estate lessors with respect to any 
aspect of residential dwelling units, including rental pricing, fees, or any other rental terms.
